component.name: Mixel Remote
component.summary: Remote support and access for your devices

description.p: Connect to your company's computers and phones, or let a technician help on this computer, with consent for every session.

Deep reliability, memory-safety, and security hardening release across macOS, Windows, Linux, and the signaling broker: fixes Ctrl+V/Cmd+V stuck V key & modifier loss on all 3 platforms, fixes Windows Media Foundation COM shutdown-before-Release UAF & Direct3D VRAM/session leaks & UI-thread Snapshot deadlock & async Drop crash & ContentDialog overlap crash & live CursorShape updates, fixes macOS audio NULL-callback race & ARC UAF & WindowCloseGuard NSWindow leak & actualSize clipping & matchLocalKeyboard Alt interference, fixes Linux GTK4 ref-cycle leak & popover auto-close & GStreamer bus error fallback & /tmp updater TOCTOU, fixes OpenH264 software fallback pixel cap & view-only Quality Mode & Windows OpenH264 adaptive bitrate, and hardens signaling broker against cross-tenant recheck DoS and unattended_host_only SwitchSides bypass.

UI polish across macOS, Windows, and Linux: prevents Status column and Unattended badge mid-word wrapping on macOS, fixes singular device count grammar, replaces the fallback '?' account avatar with a brand person icon, hides redundant 'Save device…' on already-saved recent devices, tints Account workspace picker with Mixel Red, completes German/French/Italian translations for Quality Mode on Windows, and adds Quality Mode (Auto / Speed / Quality) to the Linux GTK4 Picture Quality popover.

Adds native hardware-accelerated H.264 High Profile (CABAC) decoding on Windows (Media Foundation CMSH264DecoderMFT) and Linux (GStreamer VAAPI/NVDEC/FFmpeg with automatic OpenH264 fallback), plus feature-negotiated H.264 High Profile encoding on macOS VideoToolbox and Windows Media Foundation (100% backwards-compatible with 2.1.23 and older peers).

TeamViewer quality parity release: up to 4K/UHD (3840x2160) & 16 Mbps LAN video with 60 FPS macOS capture, 2x2 bilinear downscaling, Windows MF quality=50, in-place VideoToolbox bitrate updates, Quality Mode selector (Auto / Optimize speed / Optimize quality) & 1:1 Actual Size view, native host cursor shape synchronization, macOS AltGr (Right Option) & layout-aware typing mode, drag-and-drop file transfer on macOS and Windows, zero-copy IOSurface decode on macOS & zero-copy pixel slice on Linux, bounded low-latency audio jitter buffer, atomic Windows remote print spooling, and architecture-aware self-updater.

Allows a technician's computer to accept incoming unattended connections while viewing other devices, supports multiple simultaneous direct unattended connections to the same host, and raises concurrent session limits from 4 to 64.

Eliminates macOS screen-move and remote display-switch freezes (decouples video painting from SwiftUI layout, caches i18n bundles and date formatters, removes main-thread DNS lookups) and raises remote video frame bounds to 8K / multi-monitor ("All screens") across macOS, Windows, and Linux.

Fixes forced sign-out after Mac/Windows sleep (always refreshes via refresh_token on wake with 60 s network-reconnect retry instead of immediately expiring the session, and preserves saved Keychain sessions on transient network errors), fixes browser OAuth callback stalls on 127.0.0.1 by handling concurrent browser preconnect sockets with a 10-minute window, and prevents video pacing from cratering to 180 kbps / 540p on transient packet loss (600 kbps floor, 5 s probe recovery).

Restores seamless EarlyPicture handover on 1080p+ macOS/Windows hosts, removes LAN startup FPS throttling, adds scoped Windows 1 ms high-resolution timer (timeBeginPeriod) and sub-ms async Media Foundation spin-yield wakeup to eliminate 15.6 ms per-frame stalls, defers TCP/TLS TURN by 350 ms when UDP TURN is available to prevent TCP-over-TURN head-of-line blocking, and adds lightweight 5-second perf.log telemetry.

Major intercontinental/sub-Mbps WAN smoothness fix: lowers rate-control and pacer floors from 1 Mbps to 280 kbps (and encoder minimum to 180 kbps), scales WAN in-flight window to prevent multi-second bufferbloat, adds 2-tier adaptive resolution (1080p -> 720p -> 540p) and adaptive FPS pacing (60 FPS on LAN, 15-30 FPS on constrained WAN), caps initial EarlyPicture keyframe at 720p for 2x faster first picture, and updates Windows Media Foundation bitrate in-place via ICodecAPI without restarting the encoder.

Fixes Windows Media Foundation hardware H.264 encoder deadlock and freezes on Intel QuickSync async MFTs (non-blocking MF_EVENT_FLAG_NO_WAIT polling with 200 ms fallback deadline, AVLowLatencyMode set before media type negotiation, COM sample refcount leak fix, stream-change recovery) and speeds up WAN/NAT connection setup.

Adds native Windows Media Foundation hardware H.264 encoding (Intel QuickSync, NVIDIA NVENC, AMD AMF) with low-latency ICodecAPI tuning, fast 2x2 BGRA-to-NV12 conversion, 60 FPS GPU target, and seamless automatic fallback to OpenH264 on VMs or unsupported drivers.

Adds adaptive 1080p-to-720p resolution downscaling on slow/high-RTT WAN links (with automatic recovery to 1080p), increases ICE relay acceptance wait to 700 ms so intercontinental direct UDP hole-punching can beat TURN relay, and raises loopback auth callback header limit to 64 KB.

Fixes 1-2 FPS lag on Windows/WAN sessions: disables OpenH264 frame skipping (uses QP adaptation + 30 FPS bit budget on Windows/Linux), enables clean-line Pacer rate recovery without waiting 10s for keyframes and raises WAN GRACE to 800 ms, enables macOS VideoToolbox hardware decoding whenever recording is not actively running, optimizes Windows DXGI frame copy, and prevents clean WAN links from stalling on keyframes.

Major FPS and smoothness upgrade: non-blocking clipboard sync (eliminates 350–500 ms video stalls on WAN), zero-wait control polling between frames, 60 FPS capture/encode pipeline with faster bitrate ramp-up, one-way delay rate control (vrate2) and 100 ms receive reports, automatic STUN srflx derivation for direct UDP hole-punching on WAN, fast short-circuit damage detection, zero-copy BGRA-to-YUV conversion, and lower UI polling overhead.

Complete DE/FR/IT translations across macOS, Windows, and Linux, Linux Quick Support hosted End Session button and Recent Connections in Sessions, plus signaling broker scalability fixes (dedicated renew slots, 1/s global expire sweep, bounded renewal history).

Full security, reliability, and UI/UX bug-hunt release: hardens Quick Support claim and Save Device permissions (SQL 034), prevents failed transport renewals or key-repeat bursts from closing active sessions, fixes prewarm fallback and clip-same SDP negotiation, ensures macOS Accessibility is requested at startup, fixes hosted-session End button, and cleans up Save Device defaults.
Fixes sessions disconnecting ~5 seconds after connecting when early video hands over to the main video stream on the same transport.
Instant sign-in after launch or updates without flashing the sign-in screen, fixes macOS UI freezes from repeated permission checks, and only offers to save unsaved devices after a session.

Fixes sessions that dropped a few seconds after connecting between different app versions. Much faster sessions on local networks (no more 1–9 FPS), macOS permissions requested at start before the ID is shown, every connected ID kept in Recent, and a Save device prompt (Device Name, Company, User) after each session.

Unified 2.1.6 Quick Support app (no admin or account required), full-screen Connect by ID fix on macOS, direct Connect from the Search box, and attended Quick Support connection for all authenticated users.
Direct UDP + STUN/TURN low-latency transport, instant early-picture capture/encoder handover, frame queue coalescing, and saved device removal for all authorized admins.
Preserves modifier keys during automatic clipboard sync, enables clipboard by default in attended sessions, and maps macOS Command shortcuts to Control on Windows/Linux hosts.
Automatic bidirectional clipboard sync and reliable Command/Control copy-paste shortcuts across remote sessions.
Fixes a launch crash on macOS and keeps all desktop apps on version 2.1.2.
Faster connect: the first picture appears sooner after you connect.
New console: sessions in tabs, device administration, signed remote commands.
Files can be sent again over slow, distant connections (2.0.17 could not open the file channel there). A Mac being helped shows one pointer.
Connections open faster (secure handshake and channels no longer wait a full second for a lost first packet). A Mac being helped shows one pointer instead of two.

Sessions open faster through the relay and the picture stays smooth on slow connections. Unattended access without a question only for technicians your company allows it; others are asked. Turning unattended access off is kept.

Unattended access stays on and accepts connections without a prompt. A support password stays until you turn it off and can be used every time. The connection stays up instead of dropping after a minute or two.
Large pictures are sent at a pace a slow connection can carry. The dialog that asks whether someone may connect no longer logs toolkit errors when an option is ticked.
After "Add this computer" no wrong "already registered" message any more. A Mac can be helped from Linux (its picture no longer ends the session); pictures arrive faster.
A slow or late answer to an input or the clipboard no longer ends the session.
Session reports can be exported as PDF. Clipboard, a second technician and switching sides verified between two Linux computers.
The native Linux app (GTK 4 and libadwaita).
